chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: The Rhythm Club: pool tables, gamblers and John Hammond
summary: Danny explains the Rhythm Club, a dive with pool tables and back-room gamblers, the musicians' headquarters where he first saw John Hammond.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Because everybody would be waitin' around him.
The Rhythm Club was a club... They had one called the Band Box first. It was a little small club which

had two pool tables on the side, and a gambling house where they played poker -- two or three tables hidden behind a door. It was just a...a third-rate, run-of-the-mill dive, in other words. Just a club. All kinds of nefarious characters walking in and out, with sharp-eyed cats, hustlers, gamblers, second-story men. Everybody's gambling'.

And the musicians, they're there, and they used the musicians always as a front. They'd say it's a musicians' club. But the musicians, maybe, say, five percent of them would get into the game. But in the back was the cold-blooded hustlers playin' Skin and...I guess any kind of game of chance you'd want. And just a few of the musicians joined them games. But that was the musicians' headquarters.
Now, they've got two pool tables in the Rhythm Club and...
These are Black musicians, of course.
Well, some Whites would come around. It's the first time I saw John Hammond, around the Rhythm Club. Young White boy with the crew-cut haircut.
